 Judgment

This Civil Miscellaneous Appeal has been filed by the appellants/petitioners challenging the quantum of compensation granted by the Tribunal in the award dated 23.12.2021, made in M.C.O.P.
No.108 of 2019 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal/Sub Court, Panruti.

sentences.text: 2.The appellants filed M.C.O.P. No.108 of 2019 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal/Sub Court, Panruti claiming a sum of Rs.30,00,000/- as compensation for the death of one Rajendran, who died in an accident that took place on 16.01.2019.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal/Sub Court, Panruti
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. According to the appellants, on 16.01.2019, when the deceased Rajendran was riding a two wheeler i.e., TVS XL bearing Regn.No.TN 31 BL 7526 from Panruti to Kumbakonam on the National Highway, a Government Bus bearing Reg.No.TN 68 N 0432, belonging to the respondent/Transport Corporation came in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the two wheeler, TVS XL and caused the accident.
In the accident, the said _____ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Rajendran died and hence, the appellants filed claim petition claiming compensation against the respondent.

4. The respondent/State Transport Corporation filed counter statement and denied all the averments made by the appellants in the claim petition and stated that the accident occurred only due to the negligent act of the rider of the two wheeler who tried to overtake the bus and invited the accident; that the petition was not maintainable since the owner and insurer of the vehicle of the deceased were not impleaded in the claim petition.

The respondent also denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and stated that in any event, the total compensation claimed by the appellants are excessive and prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
5.
Before the Tribunal, the appellants examined two witnesses as P.W.1 & P.W.2 and marked six documents as Exs.P.1 to P.6.

The respondent examined the driver of the bus as R.W.1 and marked the Motor Vehicle Inspector's report as Ex.R1.
_____ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 6.

The Tribunal after considering the oral and documentary evidence held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the bus belonging to the respondent and fixed 90%
negligence on the driver of the bus and 10% contributory negligence on the deceased for not wearing helmet at the time of accident and directed the respondent to pay a sum of Rs.8,40,960/- as compensation to the appellants.
7. Aggrieved by the said award, the appellants have preferred the instant appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.

8. Learned counsel appearing for the appellants submitted the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is meagre; that the Tribunal had taken a notional income of Rs.8000/- per month for an accident that took place in the year 2019; that applying the formula given by the Division Bench of this Court in Andal and others vs. Avinan Kannan and another reported in 2019 (1) TN MAC 54 (DB), and considering the Cost Inflation Index, the notional income ought to have been fixed as Rs.14,000/- per month.

entities.text: Andal and others vs. Avinan Kannan and another reported in 2019 (1) TN MAC 54 (DB)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The learned counsel further submitted that the Tribunal had already deducted 10% _____ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis towards contributory negligence and that they have not challenged the said finding; that as regard the quantum of compensation under the other heads is just and reasonable and the appellants have no grievance about that and hence,
prayed for enhancement of the compensation.

2 9.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the respondent/Transport Corporation, per contra, submitted that the deceased did not have a valid driving license and also did not wear helmet at the time of the accident, however, the Tribunal had fixed only 10% towards contributory negligence on the deceased and this Court had held in similar circumstances that 20% contributory negligence should be fixed on the deceased for not wearing helmet.

The learned counsel also submitted that before the Tribunal, they had marked Ex.R.1/report of Motor Vehicle Inspector, to show that the deceased did not have a valid driving license at the time of the accident; that the notional income fixed by the Tribunal cannot be faulted since the appellants did not produce any proof of income, thus the compensation awarded by the Tribunal cannot be interfered with and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.
_ _ _ __ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 10.
Heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellants as well as the respondent and perused the materials available on record.

11. It is seen from the order of the Court below that the Tribunal found that the respondent had not examined the officials of Road Transport Office (RTO) to establish that the deceased did not have a valid driving license at the time of the accident.
Further, the Tribunal found that the deceased did not wear a helmet at the time of the accident and hence, fixed 10% contributory negligence on the deceased for not wearing a helmet.

12. This Court is of the view that the Ex.R1/report of the Motor Vehicle Inspector does not conclusively establish the fact that the deceased did not have a valid driving license at the time of the accident.

Hence, the finding of the Tribunal that the respondent failed to establish that the deceased r o d e t h e t w o w h e e l e r w i t h o u t d r i v i n g l i c e n s e c a n n o t b e a s s a i l e d .
_ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 13
. As regards compensation, this Court finds that the accident took place in the year 2019.
The appellants have claimed that the deceased was working as an Agriculturalist and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
However, the appellants have not produced any proof to establish the income.

In such circumstances, considering the Cost Inflation Index and the formula adopted by the Division Bench of this Court in Andal and others vs. Avinan Kannan and another (cited supra), this Court is of the view that it would be just and reasonable to fix the notional income at Rs.14,000/-
per month having regard to the age, avocation of the deceased and the year of the accident.

entities.text: Andal and others vs. Avinan Kannan and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The deceased was aged 55 years at the time of the accident hence, he is entitled to enhancement of 10%
towards future prospects, and the multiplier applicable is 11.
The appellants/dependents were three in number hence, 1/3rd of his income has to be deducted towards his personal expenses.

Thus, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head Loss of Dependency is modified as follows :-
Rs.14,000 + Rs.1,400 (Rs.14,000 X 10%) X 12 X 11 X 2 /3 = Rs.13,55,200/-
1 4 .

Thus, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced from Rs.8,40,960/- to Rs.13,63,680/-, break-up as follows:-

With the above modification, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal at Rs.8,40,960/- is hereby enhanced to Rs.13,63,680/-
together with interest at 7.5% per annum (excluding the default period, if any) from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

The respondent/Transport Corporation is directed to deposit the enhanced award amount, now determined by this Court along with interest and costs, less the amount already deposited, if any, within a period of six (6) weeks from the date of a receipt of copy of this Judgment.

On such deposit, the appellants are permitted to withdraw their share of the award amount along with proportionate interest and costs, less the amount if any, already withdrawn, on the basis of apportionment fixed by the Tribunal.
The appellants are directed to pay the necessary Court Fee, if _____ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis any, on the enhanced award amount.
No costs.
